lines.text: Elijah climbed Carmel, bowed to the ground, his face between his knees, and told his servant: go look toward the sea.
Six times the servant climbed back down with the same report: there is nothing.
And it came to pass at the seventh time, that he said, Behold, there ariseth a little cloud out of the sea, like a man's hand.
Small enough to miss. Big enough to mean the rain was already on its way.
Elijah didn't wait for proof. Prepare thy chariot, he said, that the rain stop thee not.
Whatever you're still climbing the mountain to ask about today, go again.

title: Word and Faith Network
subtitle: Go Again Seven Times
story: A four-scene illustrated short film: a prophet bowed low on a bronze dusk mountaintop, a servant standing watch over a flat grey-teal sea with nothing on it, a small hand-shaped cloud breaking gold light at the horizon, and a chariot racing ahead of a gathering indigo storm. A visual telling of 1 Kings 18:42-44 - the breakthrough that only shows up on the seventh look.
